newsitem.title: UK: Stolt Parcel Tankers to order ship stores via internet.
newsitem.headline: Stolt Parcel Tankers to order ship stores via internet.

text.p: Stolt Parcel Tankers said Tuesday it has begun purchasing ships' equipment via internet technology.

The parcel tankers operator, which is part of the Stolt-Nielsen SA group, said it has started using shipping internet network operator Telenor Marlink to electronically order supplies for its fleet of 96 owned and operated vessels.
Stolt Parcel Tankers vice president of purchasing and materials management Ken Bloom said: "Marlink offers a specific business to business market place for the global marine industry."
"I expect tens of millions of dollars worth of business will be done through Marlink for Stolt alone," he added.
Bloom said 60 ships' suppliers had signed up to Marlink, out of the network's total 250 sites.

He added that Stolt had been testing the system since May and "had gone live with one supplier last week." Cutting paperwork out of parts and supplies ordering, delivery and invoicing would reduce operating costs, he said.
Marlink President Gunnar Brand said the Norwegian group has invested Norwegian kroner 100 million in setting up its network which he described as aiming to be a "global shipping mall".
Brand said average subscription costs for Marlink would range from a low of $100 to around $250 depending on service options.

London shipbroking group Simpson Spence & Young (SSY) said at the same press conference that it will use Marlink to provide its publications in an electronic format and improve its global communications, particularly to use E-Mail messaging to replace costly faxes and telexes. --Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
